Each tap logs "The 'navigation' object hasn't been initialized yet". A restart fixes it. items.id: postgame-progress-english (MAJOR): after wm size/density reset + font_scale 1.0 with the app open, profile card / 'My player card' / sometimes a tab do nothing, 'The navigation object hasn't been initialized yet'
items.rootCause: The manifest's configChanges do not list density or fontScale, so each of those changes recreates MainActivity. The two commands caused two recreations in a row. Each recreation starts a new React root (surface) in the same JS runtime, and each root holds its own expo-router ExpoRoot and NavigationContainer. But router.push/replace/back all go through ONE module-level queue (expo-router routingQueue), and the first container whose effect runs takes every waiting action and dispatches it into its own tree. A root whose activity was destroyed before it was ever laid out never gets safe-area insets. expo-router's SafeAreaProvider then renders nothing, so that root's container has no navigator. That root was also never unmounted. Its container took the visible app's taps and dropped them with exactly 'The navigation object hasn't been initialized yet' (BaseNavigationContainer.dispatch with no focus listener). A restart cleared the extra root. I reproduced this in Jest: with the old entry and two roots, router.push to the player card logs that exact message and the card never opens. With a stale root that still had its navigator, the action is silently 'not handled' instead. I did not add density/fontScale to configChanges. react-native-svg (SvgView/VirtualView) reads the density once, when a view is created, so the app's SVG icons and avatars would draw at the old scale after an in-place density change. Recreation also comes from other changes (bold text and others), so the app has to survive it.
items.fix: New app entry apps/mobile/index.ts (package.json main: expo-router/entry -> index.ts; Expo resolveEntryPoint verified -> apps/mobile/index.ts). It is expo-router's entry-classic (@expo/metro-runtime first, then renderRootComponent(App)), with App wrapped by latestRootOnly. New apps/mobile/src/services/latestRoot.tsx: each root takes its order in its first render. On mount it becomes the newest and tells the older roots. Every older root then renders null, which unmounts its whole ExpoRoot: its container, its routing-queue subscription, and every screen and effect in it. This happens whether or not Android ever stops that surface, and a stale root never comes back. Only 'main' is wrapped; RN's LogBox surface in dev is not touched (so no setWrapperComponentProvider). No UI strings, no motion.
items.test: New apps/mobile/src/services/__tests__/latestRoot.test.tsx goes through the real index.ts, with renderRootComponent captured and qualified-entry's App rendering ExpoRoot over test routes. (1) After two recreations (Results root; a root never laid out, via a SafeAreaProvider mock with no insets; a new root on Home; then the first unmounted), router.push('/player/[id]') opens the player card in the visible root, no NOT_INITIALIZED error is logged, and the stale root renders null. (2) After one recreation, the old root is null at once, and push and back work in the new one. (3) A single root works as before. (4) package.json main is index.ts. With the old registration (renderRootComponent(App)), tests 1 and 2 fail and log the exact QA error.

items.id: ranked-end-i-surrender-my-lock-5x (minor): empty frame (only the ambient digits) ~1.5 s after confirming a surrender / ending a practice, between the board and Results
items.rootCause: This is the same race loop 6 fixed for results→search. When the game ended (after its game.end hold), app/game.tsx replaced itself with /results/[id]. On Android, react-native-screens fades the replaced screen out. But its views can be deleted in the mount batch before the posted removal transition starts (NativeProxy.notifyScreenRemoved posts startRemovalTransition). The results then fade in from 0 over nothing but the wandering digits. That matches 4/4 surrenders and 3/3 ended practices, about 0.6 s (the hold) after the board without the dialog.
items.fix: apps/mobile/app/game.tsx: openResults now pushes /results/[id] over the game (it was a replace), then calls dropWhenCovered(navigation, routeKey), the loop-6 helper. The final board stays whole under the results' flow.fade (and its shorter Reduced Motion fade). The game leaves the history on its closing transitionEnd, or after 600 ms at the latest, so back from the results goes where it went before. The game.end hold (when the game screen calls onEnded) is unchanged. Guards: a second onEnded opens nothing (ended ref). While covered, the game route's 'no game in the store -> Home' redirect and the FlowFallback report are off, so clearing the store under the results never replaces them with Home. motion.md game.end and flow.fade rows now describe the push-then-drop.
items.test: New apps/mobile/src/screens/results/__tests__/gameResultsOverlap.test.tsx runs the real app/game.tsx on the real native stack, with the game screen as a stand-in that calls onEnded. After the end there are 3 RNSScreens and the final board is still in the tree. The game's onDisappear drops it (2 screens left), and back goes Home. A second end opens nothing more, and clearing the store while covered keeps /results. On the snap-loop7 game.tsx it fails ('Expected length 3, received 2'). Updated gameRoute.test.tsx (results asserted via router.push, replace never) and ranked.e2e.test.tsx (it lets COVERED_DROP_FALLBACK_MS pass before router.back() to /game-type).

issues.problem: latestRootOnly reverses the unmount order. The new root mounts its whole tree first, and only then does its LatestRootOnly effect tell the older roots to render null. So every old-root cleanup that restores a module-level singleton now runs after the new root's setup. Reanimated's ReducedMotionConfig, rendered by MotionPolicy in app/_layout.tsx, restores on unmount the value it captured when it mounted. For the old root, that value is the phone's system Reduced Motion setting. After any activity recreation (density, font, bold text: the exact QA scenario), the global Reanimated reduce-motion flag drops back to the system value instead of the app's policy, for the rest of the run. With in-app Reduced Motion on and the phone's setting off, Reanimated animations that don't set their own reduceMotion run at full motion, which breaks the CLAUDE.md Reduced Motion rule. With the phone's 'remove animations' on and in-app Reduced Motion off (the default), the loops freeze, which is the 1.11 bug MotionPolicy exists to prevent. Secondary: keepAwake's deactivateKeepAwake(KEEP_AWAKE_TAG) in the old root's cleanup races with the new root's take. The take's async deactivate-then-activate chain probably saves it, but this is unverified.
issues.evidence: node_modules/react-native-reanimated/src/component/ReducedMotionConfig.tsx: `const wasEnabled = ReducedMotionManager.jsValue; ... return () => { ReducedMotionManager.setEnabled(wasEnabled); }`. apps/mobile/src/services/latestRoot.tsx: the parent's useEffect, which sets newest and notifies, runs after its children's effects (RootLayout → MotionPolicy). The old root then renders null and its cleanups run. Sequence: A mounts (wasA=S, sets P); C mounts (wasC=P, sets P); C's LatestRootOnly effect → A renders null → A's cleanup sets S. The fixer's own test 2 ('after one recreation, the old root is null at once') models exactly this ordering. latestRoot.test.tsx renders test routes, not the real _layout, so MotionPolicy is not covered.
issues.suggestion: Unmount the older roots before the new tree mounts. Have LatestRootOnly render null on its first commit, notify the older roots in its effect so they render null and run their cleanups, and render <Root> only once `current === order`. Or make MotionPolicy set ReducedMotionManager on each mode change without restoring on unmount. Add a two-root test that includes MotionPolicy, asserting ReducedMotionManager.jsValue equals the app policy after the old root goes. Check keepAwake in the same test.

items.rootCause: The manifest's configChanges do not list density or fontScale, so each of those changes recreates MainActivity, and the two commands recreated it twice in a row. Each recreation starts a new React root (surface) in the same JS runtime, and each root has its own expo-router ExpoRoot and NavigationContainer. But router.push, replace and back all go through ONE module-level queue (expo-router's routingQueue), and the first container whose effect runs takes every waiting action. One root belonged to an activity that was destroyed before it was ever laid out. It never got safe-area insets, so expo-router's SafeAreaProvider rendered nothing and its container had no navigator. That root was also never unmounted. It took the visible app's taps and dropped them with exactly 'The navigation object hasn't been initialized yet'. A restart cleared the extra root. Reproduced in Jest: with the old entry and two roots, router.push to the player card logs that message and the card never opens. I did not add density/fontScale to configChanges. react-native-svg reads the density only when a view is created, so the SVG icons and avatars would draw at the old scale after an in-place density change. Recreation also comes from other changes (bold text and others), so the app has to survive it. Review follow-up (high), confirmed: the first wrapper mounted the new tree and only then told the old roots to render null. The old root's cleanups then ran after the new root's setup. Reanimated's ReducedMotionConfig (in MotionPolicy) restores on unmount the value it found on mount, which for the first root is the phone's setting. So the global reduce-motion flag fell back to the phone's setting instead of the app's, for the rest of the run. I reproduced it with a direct two-root test: Expected true / Received false, and the reverse.

Each root takes its order in its first render. Once a newer root has mounted, every older root renders null, which unmounts its whole ExpoRoot (container, routing-queue subscription, screens and effects). A stale root never comes back. Review fix: the old root is now always unmounted before the new one mounts, the same order Android uses when it stops the old surface first. A root draws the app only when no newer root has mounted AND no older root still draws it. A small <Drawing> marker, rendered after the app, records which roots draw. Its effect cleanup runs after the app's own cleanups and tells the newest root, which then mounts the app. So MotionPolicy's ReducedMotionConfig, the keep-awake tag and startBackgroundWork's start/stop all run old-cleanup-then-new-setup. The first root of a run still draws in its first commit; only after a recreation is the new root empty for one commit. Only the app's 'main' root is wrapped; LogBox is not touched.
